logline: An office worker who hides her face behind an online mask becomes caught in a chain of violent, escalating consequences in this seven-episode noir thriller structured around multiple narrators.

renewal.note: Seven-episode limited series; self-contained narrative based on the Naver webtoon by Mae-mi. No sequel announced.

bollymeter.basis: Structural ambition and a committed ensemble earn it serious consideration; the final stretch loses momentum as it settles into more conventional crime-drama beats.

seasons.review_body: Mask Girl is a structural experiment: seven episodes, each narrated from a different character's perspective, chronicling how one woman's secret online identity triggers a cascade of violence across years. The show’s formal ambition stands out, along with its refusal to settle on a single moral protagonist. Go Hyun-jung’s late appearance adds an extra layer of authority to the unfolding drama. The rotation of perspectives keeps the series exhilarating in the moment, even as the second half leans more on familiar genre beats for some. As a showcase for director Kim Yong-hoon’s facility with tone, it remains one of the more formally interesting Korean limited series of 2023.

episode_reviews.title: Kim Mo-mi
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Kim Mo-mi lives a double life: anonymous office worker by day, masked internet performer by night. The episode establishes her vulnerability, her appetite for attention, and the specific cruelty of her workplace before any violence arrives - making everything that follows feel rooted in recognisable reality.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mo-mi performing online in her apartment, genuinely happy for the first time the episode has shown us - the image that gives the show's later violence its cost.

critic_note.text: Mask Girl starts superbly - all of the ideas in the world about how to portray real, painfully normal people.

episode_reviews.title: Ju Oh-nam
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The same story replayed from the perspective of Mo-mi's obsessive online fan - a formally audacious move that recontextualises the first episode entirely. The show refuses to make Oh-nam a simple monster and is more disturbing for it.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A moment from episode one revisited from Oh-nam's angle, and the audience understanding they were wrong about what they had seen.

episode_reviews.title: Kim Kyung-ja
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The perspective shifts to a grief-driven mother whose determination reshapes the show’s moral landscape. Go Hyun-jung commands the episode from the first frame, and her arrival sharpens the series’ movement into its most dramatic peak.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Kyung-ja deciding what she is prepared to do - a scene with no dialogue that Go Hyun-jung carries entirely through physical stillness.

episode_reviews.title: Kim Chun-ae
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A younger woman's story intersects with the show's chain of consequences in ways that feel both inevitable and surprising. The episode is the most genre-conventional of the seven but carries the accumulated weight of four prior perspectives.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The connection between Chun-ae's story and Mo-mi's - the show snapping its timeline into a single coherent shape.

critic_note.text: An insane thriller that keeps you entertained thanks to its fantastic performances and great plot twists.
